data.title: SpaceX's (SPCX) Next $740 Billion Opportunity Isn't Rockets or AI
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) may have another huge growth opportunity outside of rockets and artificial intelligence. In its IPO materials, the company estimated that Starlink Mobile could serve a global market worth about $740 billion. That does not mean SpaceX expects to make $740 billion in revenue. Instead, it means that is the size of the mobile market the tech company believes Starlink could eventually compete in.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

High conviction SPCX bulls now have this Tradr ETF

And recent comments from SpaceX suggest that the firm wants Starlink to become much more than a backup service for areas without normal cell coverage. The biggest change is that SpaceX appears to want to compete more directly with traditional wireless companies. In fact, President Gwynne Shotwell recently said that SpaceX plans to build more ground-based infrastructure so Starlink can become a "true mobile service."

She also said that the company expects to win some customers away from AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile (TMUS). Interestingly, SpaceX previously agreed to buy 65 MHz of wireless spectrum from EchoStar (ECHO) for $19.6 billion in November 2025 in order to work toward this goal. For reference, spectrum is simply the range of radio frequencies that wireless companies use to send phone signals. By owning more of it, SpaceX would have more control over how Starlink Mobile operates.

SpaceX Already Has a Starting Point

Meanwhile, SpaceX already has a starting point. Through its partnership with T-Mobile, compatible phones can connect to Starlink satellites when normal cell service is unavailable. However, becoming a full wireless provider would require much more equipment and ground infrastructure.

That is also where the biggest challenge comes in. Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile have spent decades building nationwide networks and control much more spectrum. Because of that, analysts believe that SpaceX may need more partnerships or acquisitions instead of trying to build an entire network from scratch.

Still, the opportunity helps explain why Starlink could become much bigger than just satellite internet. SpaceX estimates that there are about eight billion connected mobile devices worldwide outside of China and Russia. Therefore, even winning a small share of that market could create a large source of recurring revenue.

Furthermore, the average SPCX price target of $229.54 per share implies 76% upside potential. (See SPCX Stock Forecast).

data.title: Comcast Stock (NASDAQ:CMCSA) Notches Up With Private Wireless Network
data.description:
We know that entertainment giant Comcast (CMCSA) has been pivoting away from entertainment to focus on its technology side. And recently, Comcast made quite a step forward by rolling out its private wireless network, one of which it recently installed at the Smartlink company headquarters. The news was reasonably welcome to investors, who gave Comcast shares a fractional boost in Friday morning's trading.

Putting a private wireless network in at Smartlink is a good look for Comcast. Smartlink, as it turns out, handles wireless infrastructure operations for a range of carriers and tower companies. The move was intended to take the current legacy distributed antenna system (DAS) infrastructure and instead bring in a complete Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS) private network.

With this, Smartlink now has better access to coverage—no more gaps cropping up in unusually-shaped portions of the building or places where coverage otherwise did not reach—as well as a secure private network. This gives Smartlink better access to smart-building applications as well, which can deliver some noteworthy results in terms of cost savings and quality of life.

A Bad Day for Universal Studios Hollywood

Meanwhile, anyone who went to Universal Studios Hollywood recently is being advised to check their immunization status, particularly against measles. Because, as it turns out, someone who had measles recently spent the day at the theme park, instead of staying home, and out of everybody's way.

Word from the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health says that the visitor in question hit the park on July 26, and was there pretty much the full day, from 10 in the morning until nine at night local time. Given that measles viruses can remain airborne for up to two hours, reports note, that makes most anyone who was at the park that day potentially susceptible. And with over 2,300 infections reported in the United States this year so far, it is clear that measles cases are on the rise.

Is Comcast Stock a Good Buy Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Hold consensus rating on CMCSA stock based on five Buys, 10 Holds, and one Sell assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. After a 20.52% loss in its share price over the past year, the average CMCSA price target of $29.77 per share implies 17.64% upside potential.

data.title: Why Are Micron (MU) and SanDisk (SNDK) Stocks Falling Today, 8/7/26?
data.description:
Micron (MU) and SanDisk (SNDK) stocks remained under pressure on Friday as investors continued reducing exposure to memory stocks. The sector was weighed down by SanDisk's weaker-than-expected outlook and a cautious note from Citi, which warned that the memory cycle could begin cooling next year. Weakness across Asian chipmakers also added to the pressure.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

Two ETFs to trade SNDK long or short: SNXX & SNDQ

Citi Says Memory Prices Could Peak Next Year

In a new note today, Citi analyst Atif Malik lowered his price target on Micron to $1,150 from $1,400 while maintaining a Buy rating. Following meetings with memory suppliers and industry experts, Malik said pricing remains strong but is likely to slow over the coming quarters.

"We see both DRAM and NAND prices decelerating Q/Q in the next four quarters, with prices peaking in 2Q of next year," he wrote.

Beyond the pricing outlook, Citi believes China remains the biggest long-term risk for the memory industry. The firm noted that Chinese memory makers continue expanding production. While U.S. export restrictions are unlikely to allow Chinese-made memory into the U.S. market, Citi warned that higher shipments to Europe and other regions could still pressure global memory prices.

Weakness Spread Across Global Memory Stocks

The selling also spread across Asia. SK Hynix (SKHY) fell more than 4% after dropping over 8% in the previous session. Samsung (SSNLF) also traded lower, while Kioxia extended its decline in Japan as investors continued trimming positions in AI-linked semiconductor stocks.

Even so, many analysts remain positive on the sector over the long term. They expect demand for AI memory and enterprise storage to remain strong, even if memory pricing begins to cool next year.

Which Stock Does Wall Street See More Upside In?

Using TipRanks' Stock Comparison Tool, we compared Micron and SanDisk to see which stock offers more upside based on analysts' price targets.

Both stocks carry Strong Buy consensus ratings. However, analysts currently see slightly more upside in SanDisk. The average SNDK price target of $2,220.00 implies 81.29% upside, while the average MU price target of $1,560.74 suggests 79.58% upside.

data.title: "AI Reach Is Deeper Than Investors Thought," Says Evercore Analyst About Bloom Energy (BE), Stock Still Falls
data.description:
Bloom Energy (BE) won fresh support from Evercore ISI after the company disclosed a new power deal tied to the fast‑growing AI supply chain. Analyst Nicholas Amicucci reiterated his Buy rating and $350 price target, saying the latest update shows Bloom's reach in AI infrastructure is wider than many investors realized. Despite the positive analyst view, BE stock is down about 6% on Friday.

Claim 55% Off TipRanks

BE has a long & short ETF? Explore BEX & BEZ

Bloom is expanding its partnership with MiTAC Computing Technology Corp, a global server maker. BE will deploy fuel‑cell systems for an islanded microgrid at MiTAC's AI server manufacturing campus in Fremont, California, adding to an existing setup at MiTAC's San Jose facility. The move will boost MiTAC's contracted onsite power capacity across the two sites.

Bloom's AI Power Segment Is Bigger Than Expected

The analyst highlighted the growing size of the segment. For the first time, Bloom said it now works with nearly two dozen AI‑infrastructure customers, far more than the usual big names such as Oracle (ORCL), Nebius (NBIS), Brookfield (BAM), AEP (AEP), and Equinix (EQIX).

Amicucci said this shows Bloom's market is broader than just data center operators. Bloom tied the MiTAC deal to commercial and industrial firms, especially advanced makers in the AI supply chain. These firms face the same power crunch as AI data centers and are turning to onsite power because, as Bloom said, "waiting for the grid is not an option."

The analyst said this backs the idea that Bloom can power not just AI compute, but also the "picks and shovels" side of AI, including server and rack makers, chip work, and test sites. Overall, he sees the deal as incrementally positive, even though no financial impact was disclosed.

Why Is Bloom Energy Stock Falling Today?

Bloom Energy is trading lower today due to concerns over a short-seller report from Hunterbrook Capital and a fresh class-action lawsuit. The short seller said Bloom's solid oxide fuel cells break down faster than advertised and fail to hit the efficiency and output levels the company promotes.

The report cites past data showing that many systems fall below key performance marks in about 20 months, far shorter than Bloom's stated five‑year window. This was followed by several law firms urging investors in BE stock between February 27, 2025 and July 8, 2026, to join a class action lawsuit.

As a result of both the short report and a class action push, the stock remains under pressure.

Is BE Stock a Good Buy?

Currently, Wall Street has a Moderate Buy consensus rating on Bloom Energy stock based on 10 Buys and nine Holds. The average BE stock price target of $271.58 indicates a 24.55% upside potential.
data.author: Radhika Saraogi

data.title: Why Is the Stock Market Up Today, 8/7/26?
data.description:
Both the S&P 500 (SPX) and the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are set to end the trading week on a high note after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) released July's jobs report.

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

During the month, nonfarm payrolls decreased by 23,000, well below expectations of 80,000 additions. The BLS also revised May and June's figures lower by a combined 103,000 jobs. Furthermore, the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, below the estimate of 4.2% and down from 4.2% in June. However, the drop was largely due to the labor participation rate falling to 61.4%, its lowest level since February 2021.

Weak Labor Data Eases Rate Hike Bets

The jobs report was "surprisingly bad," said Navy Federal Credit Union Chief Economist Heather Long. So, why exactly is the stock market rising?

With a weaker labor market, the Fed has less pressure to raise interest rates. Lower rates are generally seen as a positive for the stock market because they decrease borrowing costs and increase the present value of future earnings. Following the report, the odds of a rate hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting slipped to 44.1% from 55% a day ago, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
data.author: Eddie Pan
